category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the video's single purpose in one sentence (sell, teach, entertain, announce, document). Every later decision is judged against this sentence.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the target audience: who they are, what they already know, what they want after watching.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the platform and aspect ratio before the first generation: YouTube 16:9, Reels/TikTok/Shorts 9:16, square 1:1 for feeds. A late ratio change usually forces regenerating most shots; occasional salvage via reframing or separate exports is possible but is the exception, not the plan.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the duration class: 6–15s hook clip, 30–60s social spot, 90s–3min explainer, 5min+ chaptered production. Duration class drives clip count and script density.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the visual medium: photorealistic, 3D animation, 2D cel, stop-motion, paper cut-out, anime, claymation. Mixed mediums within one video need an explicit, deliberate decision.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the color palette with 3–5 named anchor colors (e.g., "deep teal, warm amber, off-white, charcoal") and reuse the exact color names in every shot prompt. Color anchors stabilize palette across clips (OpenAI Sora 2 prompting guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the lighting style: soft natural, hard noir, golden hour, overcast diffuse, neon practicals. Lighting logic must stay consistent across shots for continuity.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the camera "personality": handheld documentary, tripod-static, gimbal-smooth, drone-scale. One personality per project unless the story demands a shift.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the narrator voice and language (and accent) before generating any narration-dependent visuals.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the music/mood direction: no music, ambient only, scored, licensed track. Audio locks prevent silent-video surprises.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the model set: primary model, fallback model, and per-shot exceptions (e.g., Veo for dialogue shots, Seedance for landscape motion drafts). Cost and control differ per model.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK resolution and frame-rate expectations: what you generate vs. what you deliver may differ; upscaling decisions are made once, not per clip.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK text/typography policy: no on-screen text (burned by model, often misspelled), or all text added in post. Default: ALL text in post.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the brand elements: logo usage, brand colors, fonts, mandatory mentions, legal lines. Reference images for any brand asset.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the safety/content boundaries per the trust-boundaries policy: no real person placed in a deceptive, sexualized, criminal-suggestive, or evidentiary context; no sexualized or realistic evidence-like depictions of minors; no fabricated material presented as authentic evidence (see R-08, R-264–R-267 for the full nuance).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the deliverable list: master file format, codec, caption file, thumbnail, aspect variants, platform-specific exports. Deliverables are agreed before production, not after.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the iteration budget: how many regeneration attempts per clip before escalating to the team head. Prevents unbounded credit burn.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the review gate: who signs off a locked clip, and what the sign-off checklist is (Section 21).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK file naming and folder structure on day one: `project/scene/shot/take` — e.g., `P01_S03_SH02_T03.mp4`. Unnamed files destroy multi-agent productions.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

category: Project Locks — Set Before Any Generation
instruction: LOCK the "definition of done" for the project: platform-uploaded, captioned, thumbnail set, archive saved.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Never start generation from a vague brief. If the request has no audience, purpose, and platform, write the brief and get it confirmed first.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Research before scripting: verify every factual claim the video will make. A video is a claim with pictures.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Cite sources for every statistic shown on screen or spoken in narration. Keep a source log per script line.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Distinguish documented facts from creative interpretation in the brief; mark speculation as such.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For product videos: verify product claims against the actual product sheet; never let the model invent features (it will).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For locations and landmarks: verify current appearance; AI models render landmarks from stale training data.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For technical/medical/financial content: a domain expert reviews the script before storyboard. No exceptions.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Do not invent or imitate factual evidence: screenshots, search results, dashboards, chat logs, receipts, invoices, IDs, news photographs, CCTV frames, or before/after proof. Clearly stylized or labeled-illustrative versions are allowed only when the output itself cannot function as real-world evidence; ID-like props use a fictional jurisdiction and a visible PROP / NOT A REAL DOCUMENT mark (trust-boundaries policy).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Archive the research (URLs, dates accessed) alongside the project files, so claims can be re-verified later.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: If research changes the story, update the brief and re-lock affected items — do not silently drift.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Write the script before any video generation. Generating first and writing later produces expensive randomness.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: One video, one core message. If you need a second message, you need a second video.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Structure: Hook (0–3s) → Context → Development → Payoff → Call-to-action. Even 8-second clips follow hook→payoff.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: The first ~3 seconds are the working heuristic for social retention — open on the most visually arresting, on-message frame you have.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Write for the ear, not the eye: narration in short spoken sentences, 12–18 words average.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Word-budget the narration to the duration: roughly 2–2.5 words per second of video. 30 seconds ≈ 60–75 words.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Dialogue in AI-generated clips must be short: one or two brief exchanges fit a 4-second shot; long speeches break lip-sync and pacing (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Show, don't tell: convert every narration line that merely describes into a visual beat that demonstrates.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Every scene must advance either the message or the emotion. Cut scenes that do neither, no matter how beautiful the draft was.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Write scene descriptions as shot lists while scripting: each narration paragraph maps to 1–3 shots with durations.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For multi-scene work, write the full script upfront even if you produce chapter by chapter, so chapters flow (production guide, storyboarding).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: End deliberately: the last shot and line should point at the CTA or resolution, not trail off.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For videos over ~5 minutes: break into chapters of ~5 minutes, produce each as a complete unit, stitch at the end (production guide, longer productions).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Version the script (v1, v2…) and log what changed and why; the script is the single source of truth for the edit.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Storyboard every multi-clip production. A storyboard is a sequence of keyframes with motion notes — not a nice-to-have.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Narration-first planning: for narrated content, generate/measure the voiceover first, then plan clips to cover that duration (e.g., 18s narration → 3 × 6s clips) (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: One distinct visual moment per clip. Never reuse the same starting keyframe for two clips.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Draft the shot list as a table: Shot ID | duration | subject | action | camera | audio | keyframe status.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Plan shot variety explicitly: alternate wide/medium/close and static/moving so the edit doesn't feel monotonous.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Generate a unique storyboard keyframe per clip with `generate_image` before any video generation, matching the locked aspect ratio.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Review every keyframe against the brief before animating: subject consistency, composition, style. Regenerate misses before spending video credits.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Storyboards for non-narrated content (music videos, montages) plan the visual sequence with enough unique keyframes to avoid repetition; direction may be discovered as you go.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For recurring subjects (characters, products, locations), generate reference images of each subject FIRST, then use them as references for all storyboard keyframes (production guide, visual consistency).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Shot duration discipline: prefer more short clips over fewer long ones. Models follow instructions more reliably in shorter clips (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Where possible, stitch two 4s clips in the edit instead of generating one 8s clip — better instruction-following, easier retries (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Leave head and tail room in each clip (0.5–1s of ambience) so cuts have handles and the audio tail is never dead silence.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Plan the transition type between every pair of shots at storyboard time (hard cut, dissolve, match cut) — transitions are editorial decisions, not afterthoughts.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Frame-chaining is for extending continuous shots, not a shortcut to avoid new keyframes for visually distinct moments (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Continuity is the #1 failure mode of multi-clip AI video. Treat it as a discipline, not luck.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Establish visual identity before scene work: reference images for each recurring character, location, and signature prop.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Reuse exact character description phrasing across shots. Small wording changes alter character identity, pose, or scene focus (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Give each recurring character 2–4 durable anchors (e.g., "red wool beanie, faded denim jacket, missing left eyebrow ring") and repeat them verbatim in every prompt.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Do not mix competing traits in a description; conflicting details produce blended or drifting faces.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Keep lighting logic consistent across shots in a scene — same time of day, same light direction, same weather.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Keep wardrobe constant per scene; costume changes are storyboarded events, not accidents.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Check identity drift at every clip join when frame-chaining: a matching boundary frame does not guarantee continuous identity, lighting, or motion (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: When a subject drifts, regenerate from the reference image rather than patching the drifted clip.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Maintain a per-project "bible" file: character sheets, palette hexes, lighting recipe, model list, and the locked lock-sheet from Section 1.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Aspect-ratio continuity: keyframes must match the video aspect ratio; mismatched ratios get cropped or letterboxed unexpectedly (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Screen-direction continuity: if a character exits frame right, they enter the next shot from frame left. AI models will not track this — you must.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Always specify camera framing: extreme wide, wide, medium, medium close-up, close-up, extreme close-up. No framing specified = model improvises.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Always specify camera angle: eye level, low angle, high angle, top-down, worm's-eye, aerial/drone, over-the-shoulder, POV.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Always specify camera movement, because no camera direction defaults to subtle or random movement (production guide). Use professional terms: dolly in/out, tracking, crane up, slow orbit, handheld shake, static locked-off, whip pan, parallax dolly, push-in, pull-back, rack focus.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: One camera move per clip. Compound moves ("dolly while craning while orbiting") confuse motion models.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: One action + one camera move per clip is the single most reliable prompt pattern (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Match camera energy to scene energy: slow drifts for quiet scenes, fast pushes and whip pans for action (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Motion scale: specify "slow", "gentle", "rapid", "subtle" with the move — "orbit" alone can spin wildly.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For dialogue, prefer eye-level static or slow push-in; motion distracts from lip-sync reading.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For products, orbit and parallax moves showcase dimensionality; static shots hide it.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For landscapes, drone/aerial and lateral tracking produce the strongest parallax depth cues.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: POV shots: state "POV shot of [character]" and describe what the hands/body should do at frame edges, or limbs will be missing or malformed.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Whip pans and crash zooms read as comedy/energy; use deliberately, never by accident.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Handheld: specify "subtle handheld shake" or "intense documentary handheld" — degree matters.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Rack focus (foreground→background focus shift) is a strong, reliable cue; name both planes ("focus shifts from the dewdrop to the distant barn").
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Lens language: macro, wide-angle, telephoto compression, fisheye, tilt-shift, anamorphic flare — models respond to these terms (Google Veo docs list focus/lens effects as a prompt element).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Specify depth of field explicitly: "shallow focus, background blurred" or "deep focus, everything sharp" (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Avoid describing impossible camera physics (through walls, instant teleport) — outputs morph or warp to comply.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For image-to-video, camera direction is even more important: the model already has the frame, so your prompt's main job is motion and camera (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Shot/reverse-shot pattern for conversations: describe both setups as separate clips with matched eyelines.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: When a camera move fails repeatedly, invert strategy: keep the camera static and let the subject move. Static camera + subject motion is the most robust combination in current models.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Always specify lighting direction: front-lit, side-lit, backlit/rim-lit, top-lit, underlit.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Always specify lighting quality: soft diffused, hard directional, dappled, practical sources (lamps, neon), natural window light.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Always specify time of day when outdoors: dawn, sunrise, midday, golden hour, dusk, night. Time of day is a color-temperature instruction.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Name color temperature and mood: "warm amber tones", "cool blue tones", "muted orange", "desaturated pastels" (Google Veo docs ambiance examples).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Use your 3–5 locked color anchors in prompts; named colors stabilize palette across shots (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Backlight + haze reads cinematic; front-flash reads amateur. Choose deliberately.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For noir/thriller: hard key, deep shadows, single practical source. For romance/comedy: soft wrap, high-key fill.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Specify what the light does to the subject ("rim light traces her silhouette") — models render described light behavior, not just light names.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Keep lighting continuity across a scene's shots (same setup logic), per OpenAI Sora 2 guide continuity advice.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: In image-to-video, lighting is inherited from the keyframe — fix lighting in the image, then describe only lighting changes ("clouds part, sunlight floods the valley").
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Neon/urban night: specify which colors the practicals emit ("pink and cyan neon reflections on wet asphalt").
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Firelight/candlelight/torch: expect flicker artifacts; add "steady warm glow" to reduce strobing.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: High-contrast scenes risk crushed shadows and clipping — request "balanced exposure, detail retained in shadows and highlights".
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Skin tones: specify undertone and lighting interaction for close-ups ("soft key flattering her deep brown skin").
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Weather is lighting: fog diffuses, rain saturates color and adds specular highlights, snow bounces fill light. Specify weather to control light.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Specify subject placement: centered, rule-of-thirds left/right, foreground/background layers.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Describe the frame in layers — foreground element, midground subject, background depth — layered prompts produce dimensional images.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Negative space: state where text or product messaging will sit in post; compose with breathing room for it.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Headroom and lead room: describe them for people in motion ("leaving lead room as she walks frame right").
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Symmetry reads as formal/powerful; asymmetry reads as natural/tense. Choose consciously.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Props and set dressing must be described or the model invents them — and invents them inconsistently across clips.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Crowds: describe density and behavior ("sparse morning commuters", "packed cheering stadium") — vague "crowd" produces molten people at distance.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Text in scene (signs, labels, screens): models misspell. Either avoid, or describe exactly and verify — the rule of thumb is quoted words need checking before delivery (media skill, images).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Hands, feet, ears, glasses: high-risk anatomy zones. Compose to minimize, or describe precisely.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Mirrors and reflections: expect artifacts; avoid unless the shot is about the reflection.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Food: describe texture cues ("glistening", "steam rising") — appetizing food is texture, not shape.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Vehicles and machines: specify era and model style; models blend designs otherwise.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Architecture: specify era and material to keep buildings consistent across shots.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For 9:16 vertical: compose for vertical attention — single subject dominance, centered or upper-third faces, lower-third text space.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For 16:9 landscape: use horizontal layering and leading lines; avoid tall isolated subjects lost in frame.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Describe action in sequential beats with counts: "she takes three steps, pauses, pulls the curtain aside" — beats and counts give the model timing structure (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: One primary action per clip. Two actions maximum for short clips, written as ordered beats.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Use concrete observable verbs, not summaries: "wipes sweat from his brow with his forearm" not "reacts to heat" (OpenAI Sora 2 guide: visible nouns and verbs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Specify action speed: "slowly", "briskly", "explosively" — timing adverbs are motion instructions.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Specify what the subject does at the END of the clip, or the model will loop or freeze awkwardly.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Avoid actions requiring precise object manipulation (writing, typing exact text, dealing cards, tying laces) — current models fumble fine motor control.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Complex physical interactions (fighting, dancing in sync, sports) are high-risk: break into single-beat clips.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Water, fire, smoke, cloth, hair: physically complex media — describe their specific behavior ("smoke curls slowly upward", "fabric ripples in the wind").
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Physics violations to expect and check: objects passing through surfaces, sudden appearance/disappearance, gravity errors, population changes mid-shot.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Crowds and background people: check for melting faces, extra limbs, teleporting extras in EVERY review pass.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Walking is reliable; running is mostly reliable; complex gymnastics are not. Stage action complexity accordingly.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Specify "no morphing, no warping" expectations in review, and check rigid objects (chairs, cars, buildings) for deformation throughout the clip (media skill, Veo guidance).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Continuity of props: if a character holds a coffee cup, check it exists in every frame and doesn't change color/hand.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For slow motion, describe the event at normal speed and add "slow motion" style treatment; models handle the retiming cue.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Loops: if you want a seamless loop, describe the final state as identical to the initial state and use first/last-frame matching where the model supports it.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Set overall visual style FIRST in the prompt, then shot details — style established early governs everything after (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Use film-stock and era language for live-action looks: "1970s 35mm film", "16mm black-and-white", "IMAX-scale epic", "super 8 home video" (OpenAI Sora 2 guide examples).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Use animation-medium language for stylized looks: "3D animated feature style", "hand-drawn cel animation", "stop-motion felt puppets", "paper cut-out animation" (Google Veo docs list animation styles).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Skip quality slogans — "masterpiece", "8K", "best quality" do not specify content and do not set output resolution (production guide, image prompts).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Name a reference look precisely: "shot like a nature documentary" is a style instruction that changes camera behavior, not just color.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Genre carries camera rules: horror = slow reveals and negative space; comedy = wider framing and timing; documentary = handheld and observational.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Avoid stacking contradictory styles ("photorealistic anime") — pick one dominant register per project.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Texture words carry style: "grainy", "glossy", "matte", "weathered", "pristine" — surfaces communicate style more than adjectives like "beautiful".
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Consistency beats novelty: a coherent single style across all clips outperforms a mix of impressive looks.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For brand work, style derives from the brand's visual system (colors, tone, typography feel) — never impose an unrelated cinematic style on an explicit brief (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: The master shot-prompt order: **Objective/shot intent → Subject + references → Action beats → Setting → Framing + camera movement → Lighting + visual treatment → Timing → Audio/dialogue → Continuity constraints.** (Advisor-endorsed structure.)
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Write the prompt as a creative brief for a cinematographer who has not seen your storyboard — missing details leave the model room to improvise (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: A prompt is a wish list, not a contract: more detail = more control and consistency; less detail = more variation. Choose per shot (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Order the prompt so the most important elements come first — widely recommended practitioner guidance (fal.ai Sora 2 Pro tips); treat it as a working convention rather than a verified mechanism.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Keep prompts specific but not overloaded — over-stuffed prompts with too many simultaneous actions degrade all of them (theprotec.com Veo/Kling prompting analysis).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Separate concerns structurally where the model supports it: prose scene description, then a "Cinematography:" block, then "Actions:", then "Dialogue:" (OpenAI Sora 2 template).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Keep prose and parameters separate: resolution, duration, aspect ratio, and references are API/tool parameters — writing them in prose does not enforce them (OpenAI Sora 2 guide; media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Specify what the viewer notices first in the frame — it's a priority instruction for attention.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For multi-shot prompts (where supported), keep each shot block distinct with one camera setup, one subject action, one lighting recipe per block (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Write for the model you use. Practitioner-reported prompt-shape preferences (Runway concise; Veo/Sora structured detail; Kling subject + movement + style — invideo and mstudio comparisons) are starting points to verify against your own results, not guaranteed rules.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Iterate in small steps: small changes to camera, lighting, or action change the result substantially — change one variable per retry so you learn what worked (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Same prompt, different results: regeneration is a feature. Use takes, don't fight variance; keep the best take and log it.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Keep a prompt log per clip: prompt text, model, parameters, seed/take, verdict. Prompt logs turn failures into team learning.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: When a prompt fails twice, rewrite it — don't rerun it a third time hoping (production-guide economics; iteration budget L-17).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: The strongest failure-recovery pattern: simplify. Cut to one action, one move, one light source, regenerate, then re-add detail.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Image-to-video is the default path for controlled shots: the keyframe sets subject, framing, and style; the prompt only adds motion (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For image-to-video, describe ONLY motion and changes — don't re-describe the image. Redescribing its contents can reduce motion or produce unexpected results (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: A strong keyframe with a weak video prompt produces static, lifeless output — the video prompt must carry the motion (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Separate vendor capability from your actual route. Vendor API: Veo 3.1 accepts up to three reference images for subject consistency (Google Veo docs, verified Oct 2026). This team's tool route: a single starting image, and if several are supplied only the last is used (media skill). Always check the route you are actually calling — a vendor feature is not available through every integration.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: State each reference image's role by position ("image 1 is the product, image 2 is the lighting reference") where multi-reference is supported (media skill, images).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: First/last-frame control is a vendor API capability (Veo 3.1 `image` + `lastFrame`, Google Veo docs, verified Oct 2026): defining both frames gives strong shot-composition control as the model interpolates between them. This team's tool route does not expose `lastFrame` — verify your interface before promising this control.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Choose the starting image closest to the desired FIRST scene — the model animates from it (Google Veo docs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: User photos that aren't cinematic can be transformed first: `generate_image` with the photo as reference to create a clean video starting frame, then animate (production guide, image transformation).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: If a scene needs more references than the model accepts, combine them into a single keyframe first, then animate that keyframe (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Aspect ratio of the keyframe must match the target video; prepare crops or letterboxing before animation when exact proportions matter (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Frame-chaining procedure: generate clip → extract last frame (`ffmpeg -sseof -0.1 -i clip.mp4 -frames:v 1 -q:v 2 last-frame.jpg`) → feed as the next starting image with a continuation prompt describing how the scene continues (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Write continuation prompts naturally: clip 1 "a woman walking through a forest" → clip 2 "she reaches a clearing and looks up at the sky" (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Inspect every join for identity, lighting, and motion continuity; a matching boundary frame does not guarantee a continuous-looking shot (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Frame-chaining suits continuous motion, ambient shots, gradual transitions, establishing shots — not distinct story beats (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Video extension (where supported, e.g., Veo 3.1 extend): the process finalizes the last second (24 frames) and continues action; the voice must be present in the last 1 second to be extended with audio (Google Veo docs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo prompt elements: subject, action, style, camera positioning/motion, composition, focus/lens effects, ambiance — Google's own recommended checklist (Google Veo docs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo dialogue: put exact speech in quotation marks and attribute it — `"This must be the key," he murmured` (Google Veo docs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo sound effects: describe sounds explicitly — "tires screeching loudly, engine roaring" (Google Veo docs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo ambience: describe the environment's soundscape — "a faint, eerie hum resonates in the background" (Google Veo docs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo can hallucinate unwanted audio (e.g., audience laughter) when ambient sound is undefined — always define the soundscape (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo native audio is not guaranteed: check lip sync, word accuracy, timing, and that silence is actually silent (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo safety blocks: generation may be blocked by safety filters; blocked generations are not charged (Google Veo docs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo starting from an image does not guarantee faces, text, or lighting stay unchanged — inspect through the entire clip (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Veo image-to-video suits animating objects, drawings, paintings, and adding movement/sound to nature scenes (Google Veo docs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Sora follows instructions more reliably in shorter clips — prefer 4–8s shots and stitch (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Sora dialogue timing: a 4-second shot fits one or two short exchanges; long complex speeches break sync and pacing (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Sora color anchors: name 3–5 colors to stabilize palette across shots (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Sora character continuity: keep descriptions consistent, reuse phrasing, don't mix competing traits (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Sora shot blocks: one camera setup, one action, one lighting recipe per block; multiple blocks per prompt are valid (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Sora extensions: up to 20s per extension, up to six extensions, 120s total per video (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Sora parameters (seconds: 4/8/12/16/20, resolution, references) are API settings, not prose (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Seedance 2.0: 720p default (1080p costs more), fixed 16:9, durations 4/6/8/12s, one starting image (last supplied wins), `audio: false` not honored — strip audio in post if silence is needed (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Seedance 2.5: up to 30s duration and up to 30 reference images, honors aspect ratio and audio settings; costs more than 2.0 and is not a guaranteed quality upgrade (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: MiniMax H3: up to 2K output, opening image or opening/final pair; image-to-video inherits the opening image's aspect ratio; native audio always generated and cannot be disabled (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Every model has different prompt-shape preferences (Runway concise; Kling subject+motion+style; Veo/Sora structured detail) — adapt prompt shape per model, don't reuse one prompt verbatim across models (invideo/mstudio comparisons).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Duration and reference-image limits differ per model and per tool wrapper — check the tool's current docs, not vendor marketing pages (media skill warning).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Decide the audio strategy per project: native model audio, TTS voiceover, or both layered (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Native video audio strategy: describe dialogue, sound effects, and ambience in the prompt and verify the result (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: TTS strategy: use when you need specific voice character, precise emotional delivery, or two-voice dialogue (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Combined strategy: generate video with native ambient audio, layer TTS voiceover on top — environmental realism plus precise voice control (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: TTS and video durations never match exactly. This is a narration-calibration rule, not a universal editing law — normal editorial trimming for pacing (R-204) is expected; what is forbidden is stretching, speeding, or trimming a track specifically to force a narration/video duration match. Calibrate instead (production guide):
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Aim for video slightly longer than voiceover so the tail has ambient audio, not silence; mix with `duration=longest` (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Voiceover mixing pattern: `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -i voiceover.mp3 -filter_complex "[0:a]volume=0.3[bg];[1:a]volume=1.0[vo];[bg][vo]amix=inputs=2:duration=longest" -c:v copy output.mp4` (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Silent video delivery: `audio: false` lowers cost on Veo; on models that ignore it, strip the track after generation — this does not reduce cost (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Always specify the soundscape even for "quiet" scenes: "quiet room tone with a ticking clock" — undefined audio invites hallucinated sounds (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Diegetic-only audio is a valid instruction: "diegetic sound only, no score, no added foley" (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: A small sound can pace a silent shot — "distant traffic hiss", "a crisp snap" — treat it as a rhythm cue (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Music: models can generate ambient score but not a specific licensed song — licensed tracks are added in post; never let a model "approximate" a known song.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Dialogue clips: keep speaker labels consistent and turns alternating so lines bind to the right character's gestures (OpenAI Sora 2 guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Check lip sync on every dialogue clip before locking it (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Audio loudness: normalize to platform standards in the final export. -14 LUFS is a common streaming/social starting target, not a verified universal — check the current spec for each delivery platform.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Audio continuity across cuts: ambience should flow across the cut even when the picture changes — design sound to smooth the edit.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Negative prompts suppress four families of problems: quality artifacts (blur, flicker), unwanted styles, unwanted objects, and unwanted camera behavior (invideo negative-prompt guidance).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Use negative prompts where the model supports them; where it doesn't, convert the negative into a positive instruction ("clean single face" instead of "no extra faces").
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: The recurring artifact list to check on EVERY clip review: morphing faces, extra/missing limbs, melting hands, warped text, flicker, ghosting, duplicated people, object pass-through, identity drift, subtitle hallucination, unintended camera shake.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Curated negative-prompt starters (adapt per model): "text, subtitles, watermark, logo, distorted hands, extra limbs, deformed face, morphing, flickering, blurry, low quality, jittery motion, duplicated subject" (geratools/LTX negative-prompt guides).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Negative prompts cut failure modes before the first render — use them proactively, not reactively (LTX Studio guidance).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Don't over-stuff negative prompts: excessive exclusions can conflict and degrade the positive content. Keep negatives targeted at observed failures.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Log which negative terms actually fixed which artifact — negative vocabulary is team knowledge.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Some artifacts are better fixed by prompt surgery than negatives: flicker often comes from conflicting motion instructions — simplify the motion instead of banning "flicker".
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: The edit is where AI video is actually made. Expect to cut 2–3× more footage than you use.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Hard cuts are the default transition; dissolves and wipes are deliberate emotional choices, not defaults (production guide stitching).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Pacing starting heuristics (adapt to your footage, don't apply blindly): social cuts every 1–3s; explainer every 3–6s; cinematic sequences 6–12s. Cut on action — the movement carries the eye across the cut.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Trim AI clips at the start and end: the first and last ~0.5s of a generated clip are the most artifact-prone.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Never use a shot you haven't reviewed frame-by-frame at least once at speed. Artifacts hide in single frames.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: J-cut/L-cut audio (audio leading or lagging the picture) smooths every dialogue edit.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Add all text, titles, captions, and logos in post — model-rendered text misspells and cannot be revised (L-13).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Color-match clips in post: even with locked palettes, per-clip color drifts; a light grade pass unifies the piece.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Stabilization: if a clip's motion is jittery, prefer re-generation with simpler camera moves over electronic stabilization, which smears AI footage.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Export standards: H.264/H.265 MP4, high bitrate, platform-native resolution; keep the master in the highest quality available.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Stitching command pattern for hard cuts: concatenate clips with re-encoding only when parameters differ; keep a consistent export preset across the project (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Always watch the FULL final export end-to-end before delivery. Every time. No exceptions.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Keep outtakes and takes archived with verdicts — an earlier "failed" take often becomes the fix for a later edit problem.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: All typography is a post-production layer, never model-generated (L-13 restated as a hard rule).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Text-safe zones: social platforms overlay UI (top, right edge, bottom) — a starting heuristic is keeping titles inside the central 80% for 9:16; verify against the current platform UI.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: One type family per video, maximum two weights. Hierarchy through size, not fonts.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Caption every spoken word for social — feed video is very frequently watched muted (a long-standing industry claim; verify the current figure for your platform rather than quoting a number).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Captions: high-contrast, 2–4 words on screen at a time, synced to speech rhythm, not sentence blocks.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Motion graphics in post should match the video's locked palette and motion energy.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Lower-thirds and labels: consistent position and timing rules across the whole piece — viewers learn your layout; don't move it.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Verify the spelling of every rendered word before delivery — quoted words must be checked (media skill, images).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Numbers and stats on screen: display the exact verified figure; re-check against the source log after any edit.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Product identity is sacred: use the actual product photo as reference; never let the model redesign the product.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Product shots: clean background, controlled lighting, orbit/parallax moves, macro texture moments.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Show the product in use by a person, not just on a pedestal — use-case shots convert.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Never let the model invent product features, labels, or UI that don't exist — verify every visible claim (R-05).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: For apps/sites/documents, use real screenshots stitched with ffmpeg instead of generated fake screens (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Script first, narration-first workflow: measure the VO, then plan clips to cover it (R-26).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: One concept per scene; visual metaphors beat abstract b-roll.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Repeat the key point visually in at least two different ways — redundancy is a teaching tool.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Pacing: visual change every 3–6s; never let a static visual run under continuing narration for more than ~6s.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Chapter long content into ~5-minute complete units (R-23).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Do not fabricate documentary footage of real events — use archival material or clearly-labeled recreation.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: No synthetic likenesses of real people without consent — real-person rules apply to faces and voices (media skill trust boundaries).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Label AI-generated imagery in news-adjacent content; disclosure is an ethical and increasingly legal requirement.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: 9:16, hook in the first 3 seconds, single message, 15–45s sweet spot.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Design for sound-off: captions always; but also mix so it works with sound on.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Front-load visual energy; apply the R-14 retention heuristic to every shot in the edit.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Lock the animation medium and never mix media within a scene (L-05).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Stylized faces deform less than photoreal faces — but verify limb count in fast action anyway.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Animation style terms that work: "3D animated feature", "hand-drawn cel", "stop-motion felt puppets", "paper cut-out animation", "claymation" (Google Veo docs; production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Brand kit is the lock sheet (L-14): colors, fonts, logo rules, mandatory legal lines.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Tone: gimbal-smooth camera, soft wrap lighting, diverse and respectful representation.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Every claim in a corporate video is a compliance risk — legal/claims review before storyboard (R-07 analog).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Non-narrated content can be planned loosely, but still needs enough unique keyframes to avoid repetition (production guide).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Cut to the beat: mark beats in the track before final edit; AI clips are trimmed to rhythm, not the other way around.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Visual variety across the same track: rotate subjects/locations/color treatments per section.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Dialogue clips are the hardest generations — shortest lines, eye-level static camera, verify lip sync every time (R-17, R-190).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Shoot narrative in shot/reverse-shot pairs with matched eyelines (R-69).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Emotional continuity matters more than action continuity — check performance, not just geometry, in reviews.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Deliver what was locked in L-16: master, platform exports, captions, thumbnail. No surprise deliverables, no missing ones.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Platform specs (verify current values at delivery time): 16:9 up to 4K for YouTube; 9:16 1080×1920 for Reels/TikTok/Shorts; H.264 MP4 with AAC audio as the universal safe format.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Loudness normalization: about -14 LUFS for streaming/social; check per platform (R-191).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: File naming per L-19; final master carries project name, version, and date.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Archive: project folder with script, storyboard keyframes, prompt logs, source log, takes, and the final exports. Rebuildable beats reproducible.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Verify the exported file plays end-to-end after every export (R-212 analog for files).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Thumbnails: one image that states the video's promise; faces and contrast win feeds; text minimal and verified.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Captions are mandatory, not optional (R-217) — they serve deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers and muted-feed viewers alike.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Provide alt text/description for the video where the platform supports it.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Don't rely on color alone to convey meaning; add labels or icons.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Flashing/strobing content: avoid rapid flicker entirely — photosensitivity risk and a hard fail on many platforms.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Localization: re-generate narration per language (TTS voices differ), keep shot prompts unchanged, budget for re-timing captions.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Reading speed for on-screen text: ≥ 1.5s for a short line; don't flash text faster than speech.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Real people: never place a real person (celebrity, public figure, private individual) in a deceptive, embarrassing, intoxicated, sexual, criminal-suggestive, in-distress, fake political, fake medical, or evidentiary context, or imply they did, said, or experienced something they did not. Editorial illustration and satire of public figures are allowed only when clearly non-photoreal, visibly labeled, and unable to pass as a real photograph. Never alter identity attributes, body shape, disability status, or likeness unless benign, consented, and non-deceptive. Paparazzi, candid, or surveillance looks require a benign authorized use (trust-boundaries policy).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Minors: never generate sexualized imagery or realistic/evidence-like depictions of minors involving violence, crime, intoxication, clinical treatment, weapon handling, or commercial endorsement. Clearly non-realistic, benign storybook/fairytale/play illustration is allowed. If age is uncertain, treat as a minor (trust-boundaries policy).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Evidence-like imagery: same rule as R-08 — no fabricated material presented as authentic evidence; clearly labeled, stylized, illustrative versions are permitted only when they cannot function as real-world evidence.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Third-party brands and characters: no logos, packaging, mascots, trade dress, endorsement framing, or co-branded lockups unless the user supplies assets and confirms authorization — otherwise use generic, fictional, or user-owned branding. Never depict named copyrighted characters or mascots; convert to non-infringing visual attributes (trust-boundaries policy).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Disclosure: label AI-generated content where required by platform or law; the trend is mandatory labeling and it protects the team.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Voice cloning of real people requires consent — use licensed or synthetic voices by default.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Music: licensed or generated; never "sounds like [famous song]" — close-copy is still infringement risk.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Archive consent records and licenses with the project files (R-255).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Roles: Script Agent (owns Sections 2–3), Storyboard Agent (4–5), Generation Agent (6–13), Audio Agent (14), Editorial Agent (16–17), QA Agent (all sections), Team Head (locks and sign-offs).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Handoffs carry the lock sheet, the current section's rules, and the prompt log — an agent without the lock sheet is a rogue agent.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: The QA gate checklist per clip: identity/continuity ✓, anatomy artifacts ✓, text spelling ✓, lip sync ✓, lighting consistency ✓, motion as prompted ✓, audio as prompted ✓, duration ✓, aspect ratio ✓.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: The QA gate checklist per project: brief match ✓, all claims sourced ✓, captions ✓, loudness ✓, deliverables complete ✓, export verified ✓.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Locked means locked: a clip passing QA is archived and never regenerated unless a downstream failure demands it — and that decision is logged.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Cost discipline: video is billed per second; confirm before generating more than one clip per request, and put the cost in the confirmation (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: One video generation per request unless more are explicitly approved (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: If generation fails or times out, check for the output file before retrying; if sharing fails, share the returned path rather than regenerating (media skill).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Version everything: script, storyboard, prompts, cuts. "Final_v2_REAL_final" is a process failure; dates and versions are mandatory (L-19).
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Escalation path: two failed regenerations → simplify the prompt (R-140); three failures → escalate to team head with the prompt log.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: Post-mortem every project: what artifacts appeared, which prompts fixed them, which rules need amendment. Feed learnings back into this rulebook.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: This rulebook is versioned; rule changes are logged with date and rationale. Rules are amended, never silently deleted.
source_name: Rulebook Part 1 v1.1

instruction: The unit of work is a 10-second scene. Every scene spec must total exactly 10.0 seconds of delivered picture after planned editorial cuts.
check: sum(shot.duration) - planned_cut == 10
source_name: Team convention (heuristic; amend from post-mortems)

instruction: No model in this toolchain generates exactly 10 seconds in one clip. Fill each scene with a valid plan: 4s+6s or 6s+4s on Veo or Seedance; 12s cut to 10s on Seedance or MiniMax; 6s+6s cut to 10s on MiniMax.
check: plan is in TEN_SECOND_PLANS for the chosen model
source_name: Toolchain video model docs (verified Oct 2026)

instruction: Never reach 10 seconds by time-stretching, speeding up or slowing down any clip or audio (no atempo, setpts, asetpts). It always produces distorted output.
check: post plan contains no atempo/setpts/asetpts
source_name: Toolchain video production guide

instruction: Default plan is Veo 3.1 Fast with two shots, 4s + 6s. Use 6s + 4s when the scene's main action needs the longer shot first.
check: default model and plan used unless a reason is logged
source_name: Toolchain media skill

instruction: Each 10-second scene carries exactly one story beat. If you need two beats, you need two scenes.
check: scene.beat is one sentence
source_name: Team convention (heuristic; amend from post-mortems)

instruction: Within a 10-second scene, shot 1 establishes and shot 2 develops or pays off. Never make both shots the same framing and the same camera move.
check: shot1.framing != shot2.framing or shot1.move != shot2.move
source_name: Team convention (heuristic; amend from post-mortems)

instruction: Assign the scene's main action to the 6-second shot; give the 4-second shot a single simple action or a reaction.
check: longest shot holds scene.beat action
source_name: OpenAI Sora 2 Prompting Guide

instruction: Decide per scene whether shot 2 is a hard cut (new keyframe) or a continuation (frame-chained from shot 1's last frame). Record the choice in the scene spec as shot.start = 'keyframe' or 'chain'.
check: shot.start in {keyframe, chain}
source_name: Toolchain video production guide

instruction: Only use 'chain' for shot 2 on Veo models; Veo treats the input image as the literal first frame. Other models need a new keyframe.
check: start=='chain' implies model in veo_*
source_name: Toolchain video production guide

instruction: Use 'chain' only when shot 2 continues the same continuous action and location. Visually distinct moments always get a new keyframe.
check: chain shots share location and subject
source_name: Toolchain video production guide

instruction: For a '12 cut to 10' plan, write the action so all essential beats complete by second 10; mark seconds 10-12 as a discardable tail.
check: beats timed within 0-10s
source_name: Team convention (heuristic; amend from post-mortems)

instruction: For a '12 cut to 10' plan, decide in advance whether you cut the head or the tail. Default: cut 1s from the head and 1s from the tail, the most artifact-prone regions.
check: cut points recorded
source_name: Team convention (heuristic; amend from post-mortems)

instruction: Narration budget per 10-second scene: about 20-25 spoken words. Write fewer words rather than more.
check: word_count(narration) <= 25
source_name: Team convention (heuristic; amend from post-mortems)

instruction: On-camera dialogue budget per 10-second scene: at most two short lines in the 4s shot or three in the 6s shot, about 2.5 words per second.
check: dialogue words <= 2.5 * shot duration
source_name: OpenAI Sora 2 Prompting Guide

instruction: Leave about 0.5s of breathing room at the end of the scene's narration so the cut does not clip speech.
check: narration duration <= 9.5s
source_name: Toolchain video production guide

instruction: Scenes chain into sequences: a 60-second video is six 10-second scenes. Plan the sequence before writing any scene's prompts.
check: sequence plan exists before scene prompts
source_name: Toolchain video production guide

instruction: Every scene spec carries the full lock sheet reference (project id + lock version). A scene without a lock reference is invalid.
check: scene.lock_version present
source_name: Team convention (heuristic; amend from post-mortems)

instruction: Scene IDs follow P##_S##; shot IDs follow P##_S##_SH#; takes follow _T#. Never reuse IDs.
check: regex check on IDs
